preavviso.frase: If the rent increase is 10% or less, landlords must provide notice 30 days before the increase can take effect.

regola.frase: Annual rent increases are capped at “5% plus the percentage change in the cost of living,” up to a maximum of 10%.

metodo.frase: The percentage change in the cost of living for most areas is found by looking at the April national consumer price index data published by the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics. The Bureau of Labor Statistics publishes separate data for the Los Angeles Area, Riverside Area, San Francisco Area, and San Diego Area. In areas where April data is not published, March data is used. For all other counties, the change in the cost of living is measured using the April California consumer price index data published by the California Department of Industrial Relations.

copre.frase: These rent increase caps apply to most rental housing in California that is more than 15 years old, including single-family homes and condos owned by corporations, mobilehomes rented from mobilehome park management, and housing rented by Section 8 Housing Choice Voucher recipients.

nuovo_inquilino.frase: If the tenants of a unit move out and new tenants move in, the landlord may establish the initial rent to charge.

locale.frase: If the rent increase cap set by your city or county results in a lower increase than the Tenant Protection Act, then the local rule will apply.

locale_esenti.frase: Local rent increase caps do not apply to buildings that have a certificate of occupancy issued after February 1, 1995, or to most single-family homes or condos.

legge_inquilini.frase: Landlords cannot raise rent more than 10% total or 5% plus the percentage change in the cost of living - whichever is lower - over a 12-month period.

massimo.frase: The rent increase guideline is capped at 2.5% to prevent significant one-time rent increases to tenants.

arrotonda.frase: Rent cannot increase more than the annual limit. Landlords can't round up when calculating the allowable rent increase.

utenze.frase: If utilities and other fees are included in the rent, the landlord still cannot increase the rent beyond this amount even if their costs are higher.
